# Flashcards — Topic 5: Nervous Tissue & Neuroglia
**Total Flashcards:** 12

---

### 🎴 FC_T5_01: Neurone Cyton / Soma
**Category:** `Neurone Anatomy`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Main metabolic cell body of neurone containing nucleus, organelles, and Nissl's granules.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Neurone Cyton / Soma" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_02: Nissl's Granules
**Category:** `Neurone Anatomy`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Clumps of Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free ribosomes synthesizing protein in cyton and dendrites; ABSENT in axon.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Nissl's Granules" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_03: Axon Hillock
**Category:** `Neurone Anatomy`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Conical region connecting cyton to axon; lacks Nissl's granules; site of action potential initiation.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Axon Hillock" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_04: Nodes of Ranvier
**Category:** `Nerve Conduction`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Uninsulated gaps in axon myelin sheath rich in voltage-gated Na+ channels enabling saltatory impulse conduction.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Nodes of Ranvier" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_05: Saltatory Impulse Conduction
**Category:** `Nerve Conduction`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Fast leaping action potential propagation from node to node along myelinated axons up to 120 m/s.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Saltatory Impulse Conduction" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_06: Astrocytes (CNS Neuroglia)
**Category:** `CNS Neuroglia`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Star-shaped glial cells forming Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) perivascular end-feet and maintaining ionic homeostasis.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Astrocytes (CNS Neuroglia)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_07: Oligodendrocytes (CNS Neuroglia)
**Category:** `CNS Neuroglia`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Glial cells forming myelin sheath around multiple axons inside the Central Nervous System.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Oligodendrocytes (CNS Neuroglia)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_08: Microglia (CNS Neuroglia)
**Category:** `CNS Neuroglia`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Small phagocytic macrophage neuroglia defending CNS tissue against infection and clearing debris.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Microglia (CNS Neuroglia)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_09: Ependymal Cells (CNS Neuroglia)
**Category:** `CNS Neuroglia`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Ciliated epithelial-like cells lining brain ventricles and central spinal canal; circulate Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF).


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Ependymal Cells (CNS Neuroglia)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_10: Schwann Cells (PNS Neuroglia)
**Category:** `PNS Neuroglia`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** PNS neuroglial cells wrapping around peripheral axons to synthesize myelin sheath.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Schwann Cells (PNS Neuroglia)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_11: Post-Mitotic Nature of Neurones
**Category:** `Neurone Physiology`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Mature human neurones lack active centrioles and cannot divide post-birth.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Post-Mitotic Nature of Neurones" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T5_12: Chemical Synapses & Neurotransmitters
**Category:** `Synaptic Transmission`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Presynaptic Ca2+ influx causes neurotransmitter exocytosis into synaptic cleft, binding postsynaptic receptors.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Chemical Synapses & Neurotransmitters" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>
